title: Common Grace
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Common grace is God’s undeserved kindness shown to humanity in a fallen world. It includes His patience, provision, restraint of evil, gifts, order, and blessings given even to those who do not savingly know Him.
summary: Common grace is God’s undeserved kindness shown to humanity in a fallen world. It includes His patience, provision, restraint of evil, gifts, order, and blessings given even to those who do not savingly know Him.
christFocus: Jesus Christ reveals the goodness and patience of God and is the only Savior to whom common grace should lead sinners. God’s kindness is meant to call people toward repentance and life in Christ.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God shows kindness even in a fallen world. He gives rain, seasons, food, life, breath, family, skills, beauty, order, and countless mercies to people who do not deserve them.

Common grace does not save. It is different from saving grace. A person can receive many earthly blessings and still need repentance, forgiveness, and new life in Christ.

Common grace also restrains evil and allows society to function. Even in a world corrupted by sin, God preserves order, gives gifts, and displays patience before final judgment.

These mercies should not make sinners complacent. God’s kindness is meant to lead to repentance. Every good gift points beyond itself to the Giver, and every sinner still needs Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often mistake God’s patience for approval or His blessings for proof that they are right with Him. Common grace explains why unbelievers may enjoy real gifts while still needing salvation.

This doctrine also helps believers recognize God’s goodness in ordinary life. Even a fallen world is filled with signs of mercy, patience, and provision that should lead to worship and witness.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Receive ordinary blessings as mercy from God, not as entitlement. Let God’s kindness lead you to repentance, gratitude, humility, and Gospel witness. Do not confuse earthly provision with saving peace; point people from common grace to Christ.
